stem.en: Guilds often fixed prices. Which two groups did this protect, and how?

text.en: Artisans from being paid too little, and buyers from being overcharged.
Kings from losing tax, and soldiers from losing their pay.
Rich merchants from new rivals, and landowners from falling rents.
Buyers alone, by keeping every price as low as possible.

explanation.en: Guilds regulated quality and often fixed prices to protect both artisans and consumers. An agreed price means an artisan is not paid too little. It also means a buyer is not charged far more than the goods are worth. Option d names only one of the two groups.

hints.en: There is one group that makes the goods and one group that buys them.
